speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. When did you first notice the baby vomiting, and was the vomit green or yellow? Also, has the infant passed any meconium since birth?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-day-old male infant. The infant was born via a home birth without complications. The mother reports that the infant has had bilious vomiting and has not been able to pass meconium since birth. She also notes that the infant's abdomen appears distended.

speaker: Doctor
text: Has the infant passed any gas or stool at all since birth, or is the abdomen completely firm to the touch? Did the mother notice any unusual feeding issues or dehydration signs like a sunken fontanelle? REQUEST TEST: Abdominal X-Ray.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: The infant has not passed any stool or gas since birth (failure to pass meconium). The abdomen is firm and distended to the touch. Abdominal X-ray findings show dilated loops of bowel with no gas in the rectum, suggestive of a distal obstruction. Further rectal biopsy confirmed the absence of ganglion cells in the submucosa and myenteric plexus, consistent with Hirschsprung’s disease.
